lead: A singly reinforced rectangular beam has steel only near its tension face. At collapse the concrete above the neutral axis crushes in compression, the steel below yields in tension, and the two forces form a couple that resists the factored moment M<sub>u</sub>. IS 456 turns this into two equations: C = T gives the neutral axis depth x<sub>u</sub>, and the couple gives the moment. Lintels and most floor beams are designed this way.
prereq: You need the stress block parameters, characteristic strengths and partial safety factors from the topic on design philosophies and material behaviour.

blocks.text: IS 456 (clause 38.1) analyses a section at the limit state of collapse in flexure with these assumptions:

items: Plane sections remain plane, so strain varies linearly with depth.
The maximum strain in concrete at the outer compression fibre is ε<sub>cu</sub> = 0.0035.
Concrete stress follows the design parabola-rectangle curve, peaking at 0.67fck/1.5 = 0.446 f<sub>ck</sub>.
Steel stress comes from its design stress-strain curve, with design yield stress f<sub>y</sub>/1.15 = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>.
At collapse the tension steel strain is at least 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>/E<sub>s</sub> + 0.002.

blocks.text: Integrating the parabola-rectangle stress over the compression depth x<sub>u</sub> gives a force of 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> x<sub>u</sub> per unit width, acting 0.42 x<sub>u</sub> below the top fibre. Here b is the width, d the effective depth to the bar centroid and D the overall depth, in N and mm.
C = 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub>     T = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub>     z = d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>
blocks.where: C is the concrete compression in N; T the steel tension in N; A<sub>st</sub> the area of tension steel in mm²; z the lever arm in mm between C and T.

blocks.text: x<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub> / (0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b)     M<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>) = 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>)
blocks.where: C = T solved for x<sub>u</sub>, then the moment of the couple in N·mm.

blocks.text: The steel only yields if the neutral axis is shallow enough. IS 456 caps it at xu,max: xu,max/d = 0.53 for Fe250, 0.48 for Fe415 and 0.46 for Fe500 (why these values, see balanced, under- and over-reinforced sections). Putting xu = xu,max into the moment equation gives the largest moment a singly reinforced section may carry:
M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u,max</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u,max</sub>) = 0.148, 0.138 or 0.133 × f<sub>ck</sub> b d²
blocks.where: The three factors are for Fe250, Fe415 and Fe500. For Fe415 and M25, M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 0.138 × 25 = 3.45 N/mm² × b d².

blocks.text: If Mu ≤ Mu,lim, tension steel alone will do; if not, enlarge the section or add compression steel (doubly reinforced beams). Annex G of IS 456 also gives the steel directly, without first finding xu:

M<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub> d (1 − A<sub>st</sub> f<sub>y</sub> / (b d f<sub>ck</sub>))   so   A<sub>st</sub> = (0.5 f<sub>ck</sub> / f<sub>y</sub>) [1 − √(1 − 4.6 M<sub>u</sub>/(f<sub>ck</sub> b d²))] b d
blocks.where: This is the same couple with the factor 0.42 × 0.87/0.36 = 1.015 rounded to 1, so it gives a steel area about 0.3 % smaller than the stress-block route.

items: Find the factored load wu = 1.5 × (dead + live) and the factored moment, M<sub>u</sub> = wu L²/8 for a simply supported span L.
Fix b and D (often L/12 to L/15), then d = D − cover − stirrup − half the bar.
Compute M<sub>u,lim</sub>. If M<sub>u</sub> ≤ M<sub>u,lim</sub> the section is singly reinforced.

Find x<sub>u</sub> from M<sub>u</sub> = 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>) (take the smaller root), then A<sub>st</sub> = M<sub>u</sub> / [0.87 f<sub>y</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>)]; or use the Annex G formula.
Check the minimum steel A<sub>st</sub> ≥ 0.85 b d/f<sub>y</sub> (clause 26.5.1.1) and the maximum A<sub>st</sub> ≤ 0.04 b D.
Choose bars with clear spacing at least the bar diameter and the aggregate size plus 5 mm; confirm the real d.

blocks.text: Analysis runs the same equations backwards: x<sub>u</sub> from C = T, then M<sub>u</sub> from the couple, capped at M<sub>u,lim</sub> if x<sub>u</sub> exceeds x<sub>u,max</sub>.
Clear cover is 20 mm for mild and 30 mm for moderate exposure (Table 16). The beam must still pass the serviceability checks.

examples.question: A simply supported beam of effective span 5 m carries a dead load of 14 kN/m (self-weight included) and a live load of 10 kN/m. The section is 230 mm wide and 450 mm deep, with 30 mm clear cover and 8 mm stirrups. Use M25 concrete and Fe415 steel. Design the tension steel.
steps: Factored load: wu = 1.5 × (14 + 10) = 36 kN/m. Factored moment: M<sub>u</sub> = 36 × 5²/8 = 112.5 kN·m = 112.5 × 10⁶ N·mm.
Assume 20 mm bars: d = 450 − 30 − 8 − 10 = 402 mm; take d = 400 mm.
M<sub>u</sub> = 112.5 kN·m is less than 126.93 kN·m, so the section is singly reinforced.

Neutral axis: 112.5 × 10⁶ = 0.36 × 25 × 230 × x<sub>u</sub> × (400 − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>), that is 869.4 x<sub>u</sub>² − 828 000 x<sub>u</sub> + 112.5 × 10⁶ = 0. The smaller root is x<sub>u</sub> = 164.2 mm (the larger root, 788 mm, lies below the beam).
Lever arm z = 400 − 0.42 × 164.2 = 331.0 mm. A<sub>st</sub> = 112.5 × 10⁶ / (0.87 × 415 × 331.0) = 941.2 mm². (The Annex G formula gives 938.2 mm².)
Limits: minimum 0.85 × 230 × 400/415 = 188.4 mm², maximum 0.04 × 230 × 450 = 4140 mm²; 941.2 mm² is within them.
Provide 3 bars of 20 mm: 3 × 314.2 = 942.5 mm². Clear spacing = (230 − 2 × 30 − 2 × 8 − 3 × 20)/2 = 47 mm, above the 25 mm needed for 20 mm aggregate.
examples.answer: M<sub>u</sub> = 112.5 kN·m below M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 126.93 kN·m; x<sub>u</sub> = 164.2 mm, A<sub>st</sub> = 941 mm²; provide 3 bars of 20 mm (942.5 mm²) at d = 400 mm.

examples.question: Find the moment of resistance of a beam 250 mm wide with an effective depth of 450 mm and 4 bars of 16 mm, in M20 concrete with Fe415 steel. What factored and service uniform loads can it carry on a simply supported span of 6 m?
steps: x<sub>u,max</sub> = 0.48 × 450 = 216 mm. x<sub>u</sub> < x<sub>u,max</sub>, so the steel yields and the section is under-reinforced.
Factored load: wu = 8 M<sub>u</sub>/L² = 8 × 111.0/6² = 24.7 kN/m; service load = 24.7/1.5 = 16.4 kN/m, self-weight included.
examples.answer: M<sub>u</sub> = 111.0 kN·m; the beam carries 24.7 kN/m factored, or 16.4 kN/m of service load including its own weight.

traps: Using D in place of d. The lever arm is measured to the steel centroid; with D = 450 mm instead of d = 400 mm the first example would give A<sub>st</sub> = 795 mm², about 15 % too small.
Writing T = f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub>. The design stress is 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> (f<sub>y</sub> divided by the material factor 1.15), so T is 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub>.
Taking the larger root of the quadratic. The root above d (788 mm in the first example) is not a neutral axis inside the beam.
Leaving M<sub>u</sub> in kN·m inside a formula in N and mm. 1 kN·m = 10⁶ N·mm.

Skipping the x<sub>u</sub> ≤ x<sub>u,max</sub> check in an analysis question. If x<sub>u</sub> comes out above x<sub>u,max</sub>, the moment of resistance is limited to M<sub>u,lim</sub>, not the value from the couple.

quiz.q: State the values of x<sub>u,max</sub>/d for Fe250, Fe415 and Fe500.
Why is concrete below the neutral axis ignored at the limit state of collapse?
quiz.a: It has cracked long before collapse and carries almost no force.

quiz.q: Where do the numbers 0.36 and 0.42 in the stress block come from?
quiz.a: They come from integrating the IS 456 parabola-rectangle stress (peak 0.446 f<sub>ck</sub>, strain 0.002 at the end of the parabola, 0.0035 at the top). The area of that stress diagram is 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> x<sub>u</sub> per unit width and its centroid is 0.42 x<sub>u</sub> below the top fibre.

quiz.q: A beam has b = 250 mm, d = 450 mm, f<sub>ck</sub> = 20 N/mm², f<sub>y</sub> = 500 N/mm² and M<sub>u</sub> = 100 kN·m. Can it be singly reinforced?
In the first worked example the span grows from 5 m to 5.5 m with the same loads. What happens to the design?
quiz.a: M<sub>u</sub> = 36 × 5.5²/8 = 136.1 kN·m, which is above M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 126.93 kN·m. The 230 × 450 section can no longer be singly reinforced: deepen it or add compression steel.

beyond: Not for the exam. For concrete above M60, Eurocode 2 and ACI 318 reduce the ultimate strain and change the block factors, because high-strength concrete is more brittle. Search for strain compatibility analysis of RC sections.

figure.caption: The beam of the first worked example at collapse: the top fibre is at 0.0035, the neutral axis is 164.2 mm down, the bars strain to 0.0050 and yield, and the concrete force of 340 kN and the steel force of 340 kN form a couple with a 331 mm lever arm that carries 112.5 kN·m.
